artifacts.summary: 6-phase linear plan for the Phase 5 language-extension directory merge, carrying a measured namespace rename as declared scope, an atomic-batch merge phase, and the test-root probe relocation.

memory_candidates.content: When planning a Lean directory relocation in this repo, never accept a 'paths only; namespaces unchanged' premise without simulating it first. scripts/measure-refactor-partitions.py's classify_namespace sorts each module into equal-or-descendant / ancestor / unrelated, and 'ancestor' is an ACCEPTABLE bucket. A move can therefore look neutral in a diff while pushing files from ancestor into unrelated -- a regression that no gate script names as such. Concretely (Phase 5 of PUBLICATION_REFACTOR.md): merging Syntax/{X}Language/ + Semantics/{X}Language/ into {X}Language/ takes the unrelated bucket 24 -> 23, because 15 files leave it but 14 enter it from ancestor. Simulate the post-move classification by driving classify_namespace over the proposed destinations BEFORE writing phases; if the simulation regresses, the namespace rename is in scope and must be planned, measured (declaration collisions, short-name ambiguity, external FQN citations, direct importers, pinned axiom baselines) and declared -- not discovered at implement time. Related hazard: move-modules.py's resolve_move prefers a directory over a same-named .lean sibling, silently orphaning the aggregator with its citations already rewritten, so use file-granular map rows; and --namespace-map is an unscoped repo-wide string rewrite, unsafe for any namespace with many non-moving members.
